status: fixed-before-direct-replay; motivated by retrospective validation-prefix analysis
question: Can binary-monotone four-step search retain a quality advantage over componentwise eight-step search with lower realized cost?
queries: All saved 100 validation queries per cohort, budgets 5/10/20 and identical saved saliency initial supports. Already inspected development data, not held-out confirmation.
execution: Use GPU, alternate variant order by query-budget condition, synchronize scoped timings, retain complete traces and support keys. Independently evaluate final supports on the original graph. Save all outcomes in new JSON; do not overwrite existing measurements.
report: Per-cohort and per-budget necessity, sufficiency, joint success, continuous metrics, paired wins/losses/tradeoffs, actual forward calls, graph evaluations, gradient steps and search runtime. Cost differences are measured, not forced to be equal. Record overlap agreement with historical trajectories without assuming bitwise replay.
selection_caveat: Four steps were selected after inspecting development trajectories. A favorable replay is not independent validation and does not establish spectral coarsening benefit. No per-query best-prefix selection is allowed.
manuscript: No empirical LaTeX updates or default-method promotion based on this study alone.
